claims: On April 6, 2026, the Artemis II Orion spacecraft reached its closest approach to the Moon at 7:02 p.m. EDT (2302 GMT).
On April 6, 2026, the Artemis II Orion spacecraft passed about 4,070 miles above the lunar surface.
On April 6, 2026, the Artemis II crew entered a 40-minute communication blackout behind the Moon at 6:44 p.m. EDT.
On April 6, 2026, the Artemis II crew emerged from the communication blackout at 7:25 p.m. EDT.
On April 6, 2026, the Artemis II Orion spacecraft entered the lunar sphere of influence at 12:41 a.m. EDT.
On April 6, 2026, lunar observations and close approach photography began at 2:45 p.m. EDT during the Artemis II lunar flyby.
On April 6, 2026, the Artemis II Orion spacecraft reached maximum distance from Earth at 7:07 p.m. EDT during the lunar flyby.
On April 6, 2026, the lunar observation period concluded at 9:20 p.m. EDT during the Artemis II lunar flyby.
The Artemis II mission is setting a new record for the farthest humans have ever traveled from Earth.
